question: The average marks of 30 students in a class is 62. If the marks of one student were wrongly entered as 82 instead of 62, what is the CORRECT average?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net change in marks = Correct Marks − Wrong Marks = 62 − 82 = −20

Change in average = Net change ÷ Total students = −20 ÷ 30 = −0.67

Correct Average = Old Average + Change in average

Correct Average = 62 − 0.67 = 61.33

**∴ The correct answer is 61.33 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total students (n) = 30

Wrong average = 62

Correct marks = 62

Wrong marks entered = 82

**Formula Used:**

Correct Sum = (Wrong Average × n) − Wrong Value + Correct Value

Correct Average = Correct Sum ÷ n

 
 Old Average 62 
 Correction −20 ÷ 30 −0.67 
 New Avg 61.33 Average Deviation Shift 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total sum before correction = 30 × 62 = 1860

⇒ Correct sum = 1860 − 82 + 62

⇒ Correct sum = 1860 − 20 = 1840

⇒ Correct average = 1840 ÷ 30

⇒ Correct average = 61.333...

**∴ The correct answer is 61.33 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

1. Deviation Method for Errors

When an item is misread, New Average = Old Average + (Correct Value − Incorrect Value) ÷ Total Items.

2. Combined Average

If two groups of sizes n₁ and n₂ have averages A₁ and A₂, then Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

3. Inclusion/Exclusion Principle

If a new item is added and the average increases, New Item Value = Old Average + Total Items × Increase in Average.
